body:
Source/native review of proposed #2451 b035 retains lower nonblocking contrivances: reused shared metadata or a stale in-flight stdout handler, combined with unusual descriptor reassignment, can repeat a record. Normal stdout-object/target changes, aliases, rollover and settings reload have separate passing evidence; arbitrary descriptor rebinding has no guarantee. No repository os.fork/dictConfig/fileConfig path was found by the review.

Investigate actual descriptor/object lifetime before changing sink reuse. Preserve rotating-writer identity and coherent handler-list replacement. The availability fallback also requires the original shared descriptor to stay usable; unlinking its inode or losing all writable sinks is outside the retention promise. These are proposed-source/native observations, not a reproduced household or installed application failure.
title: Unusual stdout descriptor reassignment can evade shared-log sink provenance
